newsitem.title: USA: US magistrate orders release of accused spy.
newsitem.headline: US magistrate orders release of accused spy.

text.p: A federal magistrate on Monday ordered the release of U.S. Navy computer specialist Robert Kim, who has been accused of passing secret documents to South Korea.
U.S. Magistrate W. Curtis Sewell rejected a request by federal government prosecutors that Kim, who was arrested last week, be kept in jail for fear he would flee the country.

Sewell ordered the release of the Korean-born Kim, an 18-year government employee, on a $200,000 bond, which was put up by four families from the church he attends. The magistrate said the ruling would not take effect until Tuesday afternoon to give prosecutors a chance to appeal.
The ruling requires Kim and his wife to surrender their passports and Kim to restrict his travel to the Washington, D.C. area.

Kim, who worked at a U.S. Navy intelligence facility, was charged last week with passing dozens of secret and top-secret documents to a South Korean agent, Capt. Dong-Il Baek, a naval attache at the South Korean embassy.
Sewell agreed with prosecutors that the evidence against Kim appeared "overwhelming" but said there was no indication the defendant had any intention of fleeing the country.
